key_insight: Rubric-guided large language models can grade Linux/bash exam answers with near-expert agreement, but performance drops as command complexity increases.
engineering_relevance: The paper offers a practical taxonomy for deciding when AI can reliably assist grading and when human review is still necessary in computing education workflows.
method: Tested four frontier LLMs: GPT, Claude Opus, Gemini, and GLM.
Compared two prompting styles: minimal baseline vs. rubric-enhanced prompts.
Evaluated grading on a four-level cognitive taxonomy from simple retrieval to advanced system management.
evidence_signal: On 1200 real student responses, Gemini 3.0 Pro with rubric prompting achieved the best agreement with instructors (ICC(3,1)=0.888, MAE=0.10).
watch_item: Agreement weakens for higher-taxonomy questions, so complex answers should still be manually reviewed before automated grading is trusted.
paper_title: Automated grading of Linux/bash examinations using large language models: a four-level cognitive taxonomy approach
